concepts.why: The patient has a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance, consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
The patient has a history of fever and cough, requires intubation and mechanical ventilation, and has bilateral ground-glass opacities, consistent with ARDS.
The patient developed pneumonia after being intubated and mechanically ventilated, consistent with VAP.
The patient has a confirmed infection, fever, and elevated white blood cell count, consistent with sepsis.
The patient has a prolonged APTT and elevated D-dimer, consistent with DIC.
The patient has a history of nephropathy and requires continuous renal replacement therapy, consistent with AKI.
The patient has diffuse edema of the intestine, including the transverse colon, consistent with gastrointestinal edema.
The patient has a history of angina and spinal-canal stenosis, consistent with cardiovascular disease.

rationales.F02: The patient's 4-day history of fever and cough is consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia and ARDS.
rationales.F03: The confirmation of SARS-CoV-2 infection by nasopharyngeal PCR strongly supports COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F08: The elevated WBC count is consistent with infection and inflammation, supporting COVID-19 pneumonia, ARDS, and VAP.
rationales.F09: The elevated CRP level is consistent with infection and inflammation, supporting COVID-19 pneumonia, ARDS, and VAP.
rationales.F10: The bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance on chest CT are characteristic of COVID-19 pneumonia and ARDS.
rationales.F12: The prolonged APTT is consistent with coagulopathy, supporting DIC.
